title: What the scene can do: a tools route listing every tool's switch key, description, modes and full controls, active or not
description:
From the 2026-10-21 discoverability audit. An agent cannot find the ring scene's modes and sub-tools: crease mode shows only while the ring tool is active, as 'T: mode: geodesic' without naming crease; hide/isolate only after Ctrl+T; ui-state `controls` (Scene.refreshControls, Scene.java:565-593) lists only the ACTIVE tool's controls and drops shiftHeld (State.java:580-585), so Shift+H and H look the same; `ls tools` prints an empty description because no ring-scene tool overrides desc() (Tool.java:68); each tool's STATUS_LINE only reaches the log.

Add a route and `ixdar-cli tools` that, for the active scene, lists every hosted tool, active or not: name, switch key, description, status line, its modes with the current value and the options, and its full control list (key, modifiers including shift, description), plus the routes that drive it. Built from the Tool base's shared state (IX-5), not per tool. Also: the three ring-scene tools get real descriptions, the ring tool's status line and T hint name both modes, and exported controls keep the shift flag.
definition-of-done:
1. `ixdar-cli tools` lists every tool of the active scene with switch key, description, status line, modes (current and options) and full controls including shift, active or not, read from the Tool base.
2. In ring-tool it shows crease vs geodesic, the bisector, connection, the region tool and hide/isolate without switching tools.
3. `ls tools` prints real descriptions; the T hint names both modes; exported controls keep shift.
4. Tests; mvn test and test_cli pass.
testing-plan:
1. Before/after recordings of the affected routes in the scenes named.
2. mvn test; uv run python -m unittest ixdar_automation_cli.test_cli.
changes-made: New route GET /ui/tools (ixdar-cli tools, automation/endpoints/ui/Tools.java) lists every tool the active scene hosts, active or not, from the Tool base: State.toolSummary (name, lastRow, error, undo heads, mode and modes) plus displayName, shortName, description, statusLine, active, switchKey (the toolSwitchHints row or null for the default tool), full controls from addControls, and routes. A route declares the tool it drives with RouteDocBuilder.tool(name) (new RouteDoc.tool field, exported as 'tool' in automation_routes.json): rings add and rings bisect -> ring tool, regions -> region tool, connection -> connection. Tool gains statusLine() (RingTool, RingRegionTool, ConnectionTool, OrbitTool return their status line). desc() for RingTool, RingRegionTool, ConnectionTool, and also OrbitTool and DslGraphView, so ls tools prints five real descriptions in ring-tool. RingTool's STATUS_LINE and T hint name both modes ('mode: geodesic, T switches to crease'). State.controls exports shiftHeld, so ui-state controls tell ctrl+shift+Z from ctrl+Z and shift+H from H. Verified on ring-tool: tools lists orbit (default, no switch key), graph ctrl+G, ring tool ctrl+R (modes geodesic/crease, K bisect, routes rings add/bisect), region tool ctrl+T (shift+H hide, shift+I isolate, route regions), connection ctrl+J (route connection) without switching tools. Test in ToolInputReplyTest; Python tests for the tools command and the manifest's tool mapping. mvn test 610/0, test_cli 106/0. Output in tmp/tool-38-tools.json.

Rework after review: Tool holds name, displayName, shortName and description as final fields set once by its constructor; every toolName()/displayName()/shortName()/desc() override (11 tools) and the statusLine() accessor are gone, and Scene.switchTool logs 'active tool: name - description' instead of each tool logging its own STATUS_LINE. Status lines deleted; descriptions and RingTool.BISECTOR_HINT name no keys (the ring tool's click hint carries the bisector click instruction). Routes map to tools by class: RouteDocBuilder.tool(Class<?>) / RouteDoc.tool (java.lang.Class, no app type in annotations), exported as the class name in automation_routes.json; the listing matches doc.tool == tool.getClass(). AutomationRouteCatalog.TOOL_DRIVING_ROUTE_DOCS is described once from the generated registry, so Tools.java reads no annotation and keeps no parallel lists. Each tools entry is State.toolState (the ui-state tool builder, now with shortName) plus active, switchKey and routes. The T hint's switched mode is one RingTool.switchedMode() used by label and action. Live on ring-tool: tools lists orbit, graph, ring tool (routes rings add/bisect, modes geodesic/crease), region tool (shift+H/shift+I, route regions), connection (route connection); ls tools prints five key-free descriptions. mvn test 616/0, test_cli 106/0.

Direction change (user): no route drives a specific tool. Removed the route-to-tool mapping entirely (RouteDocBuilder.tool, RouteDoc.tool, the manifest's tool field, AutomationRouteCatalog.TOOL_DRIVING_ROUTE_DOCS, the .tool(...) calls, each tools entry's routes); RouteDoc is back to plain route docs. New general route POST /ui/tools/control (ixdar-cli control --tool <name> --key <label>, FireControl.java): finds the tool's control row by its key label (case-insensitive), switches to the tool first by firing its switch hint (switchTool for the default tool, which has none), fires the row through KeyGuy.fire and replies with the same InputSettle outcome as key and click; an unknown tool or label is refused with the candidates (tool names, or the tool's fireable rows as 'label  description'). Key label, not description, because descriptions change with state (K 'bisect'/'leave the bisector', the T mode hint) while labels are stable and are what the key route takes. A tool's controls are its tools entry's controls (no extra route). Tests: ToolInputReplyTest fires an inactive tool's shift+H row (switch, row, outcome) and refuses an unknown row and tool with candidates; test_cli checks the control command and that no route carries a tool. Live on ring-tool: control --tool 'ring tool' --key T -> previousTool orbit, activeTool ring tool, control 'mode: geodesic, switch to crease', mode crease; --tool 'region tool' --key Q -> refused with its six rows; --key x -> previousTool ring tool, control 'explode / collapse regions'. mvn test 620/0, test_cli 112/0.

Per the user's ruling (the coordinator's earlier reading was wrong): Tool is back to master's shape, with abstract toolName() and the overridable displayName(), shortName() and desc(); the final name/displayName/shortName/description fields and their constructor arguments are gone, and every knot and trade tool's overrides are back to master's text. The ring, region, connection, orbit and graph tools, whose desc() was empty on master, override desc() with the new keyless description. Kept: no statusLine()/STATUS_LINE, Scene.switchTool logging 'active tool: <name> - <desc>', no route-to-tool mapping, the tools and control routes, the shared InputSettle outcome, the T hint's switchedMode(). mvn test 620/0, test_cli 112/0.

Synced with TOOL-36's retirement of the tool-specific routes onto master a328b102; the general tool surface (tools, control, key, click) is now the only way agents drive tools. mvn test 626/0, test_cli 112/0.
Landed on master with TOOL-36 (13351322): the tools and control routes were built in the tool-36 worktree.
review-summary:
The tools route lists every hosted tool in the ui-state tool shape with its switch key and controls, and the control route fires any tool's row by key label through KeyGuy; Tool holds name and description as state.
Agents drive any tool without tool-specific routes.
